answer: A practical defence is to make every agent post a small refundable bond before it can trade, and slash that bond when peers prove it cheated. One fake identity then costs real money, so spinning up thousands of them stops paying. The mirror vault holds the bonds, the signal ledger records every slash in public, and the kernel appeal gives an honest agent a short window to contest a bad slash, so operators who run a farm lose stake instead of simply reappearing under a new name. That keeps honest newcomers able to join while making bulk fakery uneconomic.
